sources.entry: Pareto Security - A MenuBar app to automatically audit your Mac for basic security hygiene.

summary.one_liner: Pareto Security is a macOS menu bar app that audits a Mac against basic security hygiene checks and reminds you to fix gaps.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a security checklist app for Mac that targets common lapses such as disabled FileVault disk encryption, a disabled firewall, automatic login enabled, Gatekeeper turned off, app auto-updates not set, and automatic screen locking disabled. It regularly runs these checks and nudges the user to fix any that fail. The README lists helper URL commands (paretosecurity://...) for actions such as running checks, showing the menu, opening preferences, showing the welcome window, copying system logs, and resetting to default settings. It also documents a versioning scheme where stable releases bump the minor version and pre-releases use patch versions, and notes that Linux releases exist without pre-releases. A troubleshooting note explains how to reset Automation (AppleEvents) privacy permissions with tccutil.
use_cases: reminder to enable macos security basics
troubleshoot paretosecurity app via url commands
notable: Checks focus on the roughly 20% of security tasks said to prevent 80% of problems
Helper paretosecurity:// URL commands for running checks, opening preferences, copying logs, and resetting defaults
Menu bar app that periodically re-runs checks and reminds the user
Documented release versioning with stable minor versions and patch-level pre-releases
caveats: README mentions a Linux release, but it is not described in detail
Install and run instructions are not included in the README
README does not state a license
